newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's M1 money supply jumps 5.4 pct in July.
newsitem.headline: Israel's M1 money supply jumps 5.4 pct in July.

text.p: Israel's M1 money supply jumped a preliminary 5.4 percent in July to 19.2 billion shekels, the Bank of Israel said in a statement on Sunday.
This followed a 1.6 percent increase in June (revised down from a preliminary 1.8 percent gain) and a 0.5 percent decline in May (revised from a decline of 0.4 percent).
The Bank of Israel statement did not provide any explanation for the rise and officials could not be reached for comment.
A Bank of Israel spokeswoman said she did not know the last time M1 had risen so sharply but she did say this was the largest monthly rise at least since 1994.
The July figure brought the M1 increase in the past 12 months to 15.5 percent compared with 11.9 percent in calendar 1996 and 16.5 percent in 1995.
The sharp rise in M1 follows the release on Friday of a relatively high 1.0 percent increase in the July consumer price index (CPI). In June the CPI rose 1.1 percent.
The CPI and money supply figures are two key parameters the central bank uses in determining interest rates.
Economists expect the Bank of Israel will raise interest rates at the end of August by 0.3 to 0.5 percentage point. Its key lending rate now stands at 12.7 percent.
The Bank of Israel said total credit rose 1.7 percent in July to 290.0 billion shekels after growing 1.1 percent in June and 1.5 percent in May.
In July 1996 total credit increased 1.8 percent.
In the past 12 months total credit grew 17.6 percent versus 20.0 percent in calendar 1996 and 23.4 percent in 1995.
Unlinked-shekel credit rose 1.3 percent in July to 88.0 billion shekels after increasing 0.7 percent in June.
